title: Logical Spectroscopy: Lifted-Product Codes with Addressable Bases
abstract: Quantum LDPC memories can encode many logical qubits, but dimension alone does not make them usable: applications need explicit conjugate logical operators with structured labels and physical representatives. For hypergraph-product (HGP) codes this structure is transparent, since the input matrices are binary and can be row-reduced over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Abelian lifted-product codes are subtler. Their seed entries are shifts, or sparse sums of shifts, in a group-algebra ring rather than a field, so pivot blocks need not be invertible and global row reduction can fail.   We address this with \emph{logical spectroscopy}, a spectral construction that replaces global row reduction by finite-field computations in the Frobenius character packets of the Abelian lift group. The Chinese remainder theorem (CRT) decomposes the group algebra into these packets. In each packet, we compute kernels, quotients, and product-complex homology; we then lift the resulting representatives back with CRT idempotents and pair $X$ and $Z$ logicals through reciprocal trace-dual packets. This gives complete addressable conjugate logical bases for finite Abelian lifted products $\mathsf{LP}(A,B)$.   The same packet data also gives design diagnostics. Packet ranks show how logical sectors split, the lifted representatives give certified upper bounds on the width of the constructed conjugate basis, and whole-orbit erasures decompose into packet-attributed erased-logical dimensions. Thus, CRT packets also serve as working coordinates: they label logical sectors, certify the constructed basis width, and attribute structured erasure failures. Under bounded seed-shape and group-basis-support assumptions, this construction gives Abelian lifted-product qLDPC families an HGP-like feature while preserving the layout freedom of group-algebra lifts.
summary: This paper introduces 'logical spectroscopy' to solve the problem of constructing usable logical bases for Abelian lifted-product qLDPC codes. By employing the Chinese Remainder Theorem to decompose the underlying group algebra, it replaces failed global row reduction with solvable finite-field computations. This yields a fully addressable and structured basis essential for implementing quantum gates in fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_problem: The core challenge is developing a systematic method to construct and addressable conjugate logical operators for high-rate Abelian lifted-product quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes.
main_result: The authors introduce 'logical spectroscopy,' a spectral construction that successfully replaces failed global row reduction with finite-field computations, yielding complete addressable conjugate logical bases.
method: The method utilizes the Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT) to decompose the group algebra into Frobenius character packets. Calculations are performed independently in each packet, and results are then lifted back using CRT idempotents.
model_or_system: The work focuses on Quantum Error-Correcting (QEC) codes, specifically Abelian lifted-product (LP) qLDPC codes, which encode logical qubits for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
key_observables: Complete addressable conjugate logical bases; packet ranks showing sector splitting; certified upper bounds on basis width from lifted representatives; and packet-attributed dimensions for erased logicals.
important_parameters: The construction is valid under bounded seed-shape and bounded group-basis-support assumptions.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption enabling the spectral method is that the complex problem over the group algebra can be decomposed into independent, solvable finite-field problems via CRT.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the process flow: moving from a module problem over the group algebra to factorization into CRT packets, solving each packet independently, and finally lifting the results back to establish logical sector pairing.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the failure of standard row reduction for Abelian LP codes. It then introduces 'logical spectroscopy' as the spectral replacement, detailing the use of CRT decomposition, computation within individual packets (kernels, quotients), and the final reconstruction/pairing of X and Z logicals.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful algebraic tool to analyze complex quantum error-correcting codes by translating difficult group algebra problems into manageable finite-field computations, which is crucial for designing scalable fault-tolerant quantum hardware.

Figure 2 and the tabulated data in Appendix F illus- trate why basis width, distance upper-bound diagnos- tics, and structured-erasure exposure are distinct objec- tives. In the displayed comparison, M45 4,10 has a mod- est certificate and a lower two-left-orbit failure rate than the 3 × 7 monomial benchmarks. The sparse parity- systematic probes P75 3,7 and P91 3,7 repair parts of the trivial- packet rank profile, but they are more exposed to this particular one- and two-left-orbit erasure model. Con- versely, an attractive erasure score does not compensate for a verified small distance upper-bound witness; such seeds should be treated as warning examples rather than benchmark candidates.
